quotes.text: The EEDT serves as a virtual replica of decentralized components of the supply chain in the form of inventory systems, transportation networks, and demand nodes, and receives real-time IoT information at the edge to minimize latency.
Warehouses (capacity-constrained storage model), distribution centers (intermediate routing node model), and retailers (end-demand point model) are modeled as simulation environment.
Transactional SCM data (e.g. UCI and industry inventory datasets) provided publicly are mixed with benchmark synthetic data to model a dynamic demand, lead times and distribution variability.

GA does global optimization of strategic actions such as selecting suppliers and allocating inventory, whereas MARL allows real-time and adaptive control of distributed agents (e.g., warehouses and retailers).
Both of the modules provide a two-way connection to the digital twin that creates a closed-loop feedback process that constantly modifies decisions based on performance metrics.
The concept of supply chain management (SCM) has been shifting toward manual decision-making to intelligent systems employing artificial intelligence.
